course_goals.text: Apply the foundational concepts and optimization techniques required to build and train complex deep learning models.
Evaluate the theoretical constraints and approximation capabilities that govern the performance and architectural design of neural networks.
Understand the complete lifecycle of deep learning, connecting historical mechanics, practical training methods, and underlying mathematical limits.

L01.lecture_goal: understand the foundational concepts, history, and mechanics required to build and train deep learning models.

objectives.text: You'll be able to outline the course structure, topics, policies, and motivation for studying deep learning.
You'll be able to explain the historical context and key technological components that define modern deep learning.
You'll be able to define the fundamental structure of a neural network and compare its representational power and generalization capabilities.
You'll be able to explain the concepts of training, loss functions, and hierarchical representation in deep learning models.

L02.lecture_goal: master the theoretical and practical methods required to train and optimize complex neural networks.

objectives.text: You'll be able to understand the fundamental principles of neural network training and optimization.
You'll be able to analyze the computational mechanics of modern neural network training.

L03.lecture_goal: evaluate the theoretical foundations and practical architectural constraints governing the approximation capabilities of neural networks.

objectives.text: You'll be able to frame the problem of function approximation by defining the components of machine learning and the formal requirements for neural network modeling.
You'll be able to derive the theoretical bounds for function approximation by defining Lipschitz continuity and outlining the proof strategy for the universal function approximation theorem.
You'll be able to construct and critique the practical implementation of function approximation using ReLU networks and geometric techniques.
You'll be able to analyze the architectural trade-offs in deep learning by comparing network width and depth and explaining the role of depth separation results.
You'll be able to analyze the structural properties of deep networks by proving piecewise linearity, tracking kink accumulation, and demonstrating depth separation.
You'll be able to evaluate the practical and theoretical implications of deep network design by comparing scaling laws, contrasting theory with practice, and matching architecture to data structure.
